prompt: Where does Google Cloud keep the list of a company's people?

choices.why: Policies name principals; they do not hold accounts.
Right. Cloud Identity or Workspace holds the accounts; Google Cloud trusts them.
A billing account pays; it holds no people.
That policy restricts domains; it lists nobody.

prompt: What creates the organisation node at the top of a company's tree?
hint: It starts with a DNS record.

choices.text: Creating the first project with a company card
choices.why: A project with no organisation stays without one, card or not.
No such command creates one; the domain does.

choices.text: Linking a billing account to a folder
choices.why: Folders exist only under an organisation, and billing links to projects.

choices.text: Verifying the domain the company owns
choices.why: Right. Once the domain is verified, Google creates the organisation for it.

prompt: Why does the lesson call the super administrator accounts the keys to the whole estate, though they hold no IAM role?
hint: What can a directory administrator do to any account?

choices.text: They control the Owner's own account
choices.why: Right. Taking over the Owner's account is taking over what the Owner holds.

choices.text: They are Owner of every project automatically
choices.why: They hold no IAM role. The power comes from the accounts they control.

choices.text: They pay the bill for every project
choices.why: Billing is separate from the directory.

choices.text: They can lift any organisation policy
choices.why: That needs the policy administrator role, which is IAM.

prompt: A contractor leaves. The directory suspends their account. What happens to the roles granted to it in Google Cloud?
hint: Who decides whether the account can sign in?

choices.text: They keep working until each policy is edited
choices.why: Editing policies is tidying; the suspension already ended the access.

choices.text: They move to the contractor's manager
choices.why: Roles never move between principals on their own.
Right. A suspended account cannot sign in, so no grant to it can be used.

choices.text: They are deleted after thirty days
choices.why: No such clock exists; the access ends with the suspension.

prompt: Match each product to what it gives a company.
hint: Two give accounts, one adds office tools.

pairs.right: accounts and groups, at no cost
the same, plus Gmail and Drive

prompt: In `groups.tf`, what is the parent of the group `planner-oncall`?

choices.why: Groups live in the directory, not in projects.
Folders hold projects, never groups.
Right. A group belongs to the directory, which is why it outlives any project.
Billing has nothing to do with groups.

prompt: The group's display name changes from `planner on-call` to `Planner on-call rota`. What happens to the IAM grants naming it?
hint: Policies name the group by what?

choices.why: Right. `group:planner-oncall@example.com` is the id; the display name is a label.
That would happen if the address changed, not the display name.

choices.text: They move to a new group with the new name
choices.why: No new group is created by a rename.
Grants do not expire from a rename.

prompt: A project Owner wants to apply `groups.tf` and add themselves to `break-glass`. Why should Owner not be enough?

choices.why: Terraform is a client; anybody can run it. The question is what the API allows.

choices.text: Groups can only be created in the console
choices.why: The Cloud Identity API creates them, which is what the file uses.
Nothing reserves it; the safeguard is who may change memberships.

choices.text: It takes a directory role, not an IAM one
choices.why: Right. Keeping it separate stops project owners promoting themselves into emergency groups.

prompt: How many resources does the plan for `groups.tf` add?
In which direction does Google Cloud Directory Sync copy users and groups?
hint: Which directory stays the source of truth?

choices.text: From Cloud Identity to the company's directory
choices.why: That would make Google's copy the truth, the opposite of the intention.
Right. One way, so the company's directory stays the truth.
GCDS is one-way on purpose.
It copies directory objects; it never touches IAM.

prompt: With synchronising plus single sign-on through Entra ID, who checks Ana's password?
hint: Single sign-on sends the sign-in somewhere.

choices.why: Right. Google sees `ana@example.com` as usual and never sees the password.
Single sign-on is exactly what keeps the password at the company's provider.

choices.text: Nobody; single sign-on needs no password
choices.why: Somebody still checks it, once, at the identity provider.

choices.text: The project's Owner, by approving the sign-in
choices.why: No person approves sign-ins.

prompt: A company wants Google Cloud and nothing else from Google, and refuses a second copy of its directory. Which arrangement fits?

choices.why: That copies every account into Cloud Identity, the copy the company refuses.
Those belong to the people, not the company, and nobody can suspend them.
Right. A workforce pool trusts the company's provider directly, and no account is copied.
Service accounts are for programs, and have no password to sign in with.

prompt: Before choosing a workforce pool for people, what should a team read?
hint: Federated identities are not accepted everywhere.

choices.text: The price list of Cloud Identity Premium
choices.why: A workforce pool replaces Cloud Identity accounts; their price is not the question.
Right. Some products, mostly from Workspace's family, do not accept them.
Locations constrain resources, not who can sign in.
Terraform supports pools fine; the limits are on Google's products.

prompt: Put the steps of Ana signing in with synchronising plus single sign-on in order.
hint: The password goes to the company, the identity to Google.
items: Ana opens the Google Cloud console
Google sends her to Entra ID
Entra ID checks her password and second factor
Entra ID tells Google who she is
trap: Putting the password check before Google sends her away is the slip: she reaches Entra ID only because Google redirected her there.

prompt: The planner company signs in with Entra ID and plans to adopt Google Workspace next year. Which arrangement avoids a migration later?
hint: Workspace needs accounts of a particular kind.

choices.text: A workforce pool now, and Workspace on top
choices.why: Workspace does not run on federated identities; that is the migration.

choices.text: Personal Gmail accounts until Workspace arrives
choices.why: Those would then have to be replaced, and nobody can suspend them meanwhile.
Without one there is no organisation, and every lesson so far needed it.
Right. Workspace needs Cloud Identity accounts, so creating them now avoids moving later.
